summary: Recent updates to WebRender bindings have improved how Firefox handles high dynamic range (HDR) video. By utilizing a Direct3D 11 shader for converting HDR content, Firefox can now deliver richer colors and better contrast in videos, enhancing the viewing experience. Additionally, changes were made to ensure that screenshots taken with the graphics library OpenGL ES are processed correctly, specifically by reading the image format as RGBA even when certain extensions are not available. These enhancements collectively contribute to better video render quality and performance, particularly for HDR content, which is becoming increasingly common.
